# nakara-oss

nakara-oss is the public, MIT-licensed monorepo of FiveM resources (nakara_*) and developer tooling (@aeterna_game/fivem-devkit) maintained by the Nakara City dev team.

Every resource package declares its capabilities in oss.json (validated against oss.schema.json), every PR is scanned by fivem-devkit safety, and every release archive is built in CI with a cryptographic provenance attestation and SHA256SUMS.

## Released Packages

- fivem-devkit ({{devkit.version}}): static scanner (lexer-based, no code execution) and busted test harness for FiveM resources. Detects undeclared capabilities and dangerous runtime patterns (such as dynamic code loading or operating system command execution) in any resource directory.
  Link: https://github.com/aeterna/nakara-oss/tree/main/packages/devkit

- nakara_cargen_fix ({{cargen.version}}): Client-only crash fix for CNetworkCarGenWorldStateData Pool Full (net.dll+487A2) without framework dependencies.
  Link: https://github.com/aeterna/nakara-oss/tree/main/packages/cargen-fix

- AETERNA Game Launcher: a game launcher, written in Rust, that a FiveM server community gives its players to join that server.
  Link: https://github.com/aeterna/nakara-oss/releases?q=launcher-v
  Template for server owners: https://github.com/aeterna/aeterna-launcher-template

- nakara_rongroi (Rongroi Server Kit): Server-side kit for aeterna-rongroi.
  Link: https://github.com/aeterna/nakara-oss/releases?q=nakara_rongroi

## Packages in Development

- Nakara Tickets: Discord ticket system with in-game actions over a port-less bridge.

## What the Scanner Cannot Catch

The scanner flags suspicious patterns and points reviewers to specific lines of code. It does not provide an automated verdict on whether code is benign. Static analysis cannot catch:
- Logic bombs or destructive logic within APIs the resource is permitted to use
- Calls into other resources' runtime exports
- Server net events that trust client parameters without validation
- Values built at runtime (reported where they occur, but not traced)

Human review of the source code remains indispensable.
